advances:
This supplies the capacity input left conditional in accepted fact
`42e17c270e11ad3e`.  For every bounded fixed half-plane code arising
from the intrinsic charging rule of accepted fact
`82b3ba85b724a42f`, it proves
\(\mathscr C(B)=|Z|-|W|\), gives a rational shoelace formula and its
exact differential, and gives a finite complete list of validity
predicates.  It separates structural equalities, intrinsic
facet-vertex feasibility rows, and recoding events.  It also isolates
the full-dimensional unbounded-\(Z\) case, where the capacity is
infinite and there is no finite differential row.
author: mp_r137_rank2_capacity_code
proof:
Accepted fact `82b3ba85b724a42f` proves that, for a point in the open
singleton chamber, both transverse fan charges vanish exactly on the
region \(Z\) in (5).  It also proves \(g_j\leq0\) on \(B\).
The standard half-plane description of a counterclockwise convex
polygon therefore gives
\[
B=\bigcap_{j=0}^{n-1}\{g_j\leq0\},
\]
after harmless deletion of zero-length edges.  Intersecting with the
two axis halfspaces proves
\[
W=B\cap\{S,T\geq0\}.
\]
Since \(\mathcal J_{\rm ch}\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\), one has
\(W\subseteq Z\).  Hence the zero-charge part outside \(B\) is
\(Z\setminus W\).  The two coordinate walls are null for planar area,
so the open-chamber characterization from the accepted fact gives
(6), including every wall boundary.

We next prove the fixed-code formula.  Expanding (1) gives
\[
g_j(S,T)
=(d_j)_2S-(d_j)_1T+[d_j,b_j],
\]
which is (9).  Cramer's rule applied to
\[
n_i\mathbin{\cdot}X=-c_i,\qquad
n_k\mathbin{\cdot}X=-c_k
\]
gives (10).  Therefore every selected vertex in (11) is rational and
the incidences (15) hold identically.

For each \(\nu\), the line \(g_{a_\nu}=0\) contains
\(p_\nu,p_{\nu+1}\).  By (13), all other selected vertices lie
strictly in its inward halfspace.  Thus
\([p_\nu,p_{\nu+1}]\) is an exposed edge of the convex hull of all
the \(p_\mu\).  The noncollision condition makes these \(m\) exposed
edges distinct.  A convex hull of \(m\) points has at most \(m\)
edges, so these are all its edges and the displayed list is its
counterclockwise boundary.  It follows that
\[
\bigcap_{\nu=0}^{m-1}\{g_{a_\nu}\leq0\}
=\operatorname{conv}\{p_0,\ldots,p_{m-1}\}.
\tag{33}
\]
Every remaining inequality contains every \(p_\nu\) by (14), hence,
by affinity, contains their convex hull.  Intersecting those
remaining halfspaces does not change the right side of (33), proving
(16).  This simultaneously proves boundedness and shows why
facet-vertex feasibility is the only weak containment condition
needed.  Shoelace in the \(S,T\)-plane, followed by multiplication by
\(\gamma\), proves (17).

Differentiate the two active line equations at a selected vertex.
Their coefficient matrix has determinant \(\delta_{ik}\neq0\), so
the velocity exists uniquely and is (19).  For a moving polygon
support, direct differentiation of (1) gives (20), while a fixed axis
gives the stated zero coordinate velocity.  Differentiating
shoelace and reindexing its second sum gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
D|P|[\beta]
&=\frac{\gamma}{2}\sum_\nu
\bigl([\dot p_\nu,p_{\nu+1}]
      [p_\nu,\dot p_{\nu+1}]\bigr)\\
&=\frac{\gamma}{2}\sum_\nu
[p_{\nu-1}-p_{\nu+1},\dot p_\nu],
\end{aligned}
\]
which proves (21) and then (22).  Equations (10), (18), and (19) also
prove the asserted rationality.  In particular, the displayed
rational expression extends differentiably across an active weak
slack as long as its selected denominators stay nonzero, and it
equals the true area throughout the feasible side \(h_{\nu i}\geq0\).

For the carrier construction, (23) and \(g_i\leq0\) imply
\(g_i=0\) for every \(i\in A\).  A rank-one carrier is a line, and
substitution of (24) reduces the exact intersection to the
one-dimensional inequalities (25).  The signs in (26) make
\(t_-\) respectively the selected lower endpoint and \(t_+\) the
selected upper endpoint; (27) says that all other inequalities
contain both endpoints, hence the entire interval.  A rank-two
carrier has a unique common point, and the remaining slacks decide
whether it is feasible.  This proves (27)--(28).  Conversely, for a
nonempty lower-dimensional polyhedron, the inequalities active on
its relative interior positively span the orthogonal complement of
its affine hull.  A finite positive dependence among their affine
forms supplies (23), so the carrier codes omit no bounded
lower-dimensional case.

We now verify completeness of the predicate list.  As long as the
input edge lengths, support slacks in (29a), and wall signs do not
change, (1)--(4) give the same reduced counterclockwise polygon and
the same finite half-plane systems.  In a two-dimensional code,
nonvanishing of the selected determinants keeps every vertex formula
finite.  The noncollision and strict skeleton predicates keep exactly
the same exposed-edge cycle.  The weak slacks keep every other
halfspace redundant on the selected convex hull.  Thus (33) and the
same rational formula remain valid.  Conversely, if this selected
formula ceases to describe the half-plane intersection, then either a
selected line intersection ceases to be finite, an exposed edge
collapses or loses strict exposure, or another halfspace ceases to
contain a selected vertex.  These are exactly (12), (13), and (14).
The same argument after restriction to the carrier line proves
exhaustiveness of (23)--(27).  There is therefore no unlisted
capacity-combinatorics event.

The three-way zero classification follows from the role of each
predicate.  A declared incidence or dependence is part of the
stratum equations and must be differentiated as an equality.
A weak slack is precisely the geometric assertion that an otherwise
redundant halfspace contains a selected vertex; at equality, its
one-sided tangent condition is (29).  Denominators, noncollision,
strict exposure, charging signs, carrier rank, and endpoint
separation are needed to identify the formula itself, so their first
nonstructural zero requires recoding.  This proves both the
classification and the claimed row list.  It also supplies the
finite formula and finite validity-predicate hypothesis which
accepted fact `42e17c270e11ad3e` had left as an input.

It remains to justify (31).  If a displayed direction
\(\varepsilon Jn_i\) satisfies all homogeneous inequalities, it is a
nonzero recession direction.  Conversely, if the planar polyhedral
cone \(\operatorname{rec}(P)\) is nontrivial, then either it is a line
or halfplane, or it has an extreme ray.  In every case it has a
nonzero boundary ray on \(n_i\mathbin{\cdot}r=0\) for some input
normal \(n_i\), and that ray is a positive multiple of
\(Jn_i\) or \(-Jn_i\).  This proves (31).  An unbounded convex set
with nonempty planar interior has infinite area, proving (32).
An unbounded convex set of planar dimension at most one has area
zero; since \(W\subseteq Z\), the exceptional structural
lower-dimensional conclusion follows.

Finally, cyclic relabeling only permutes the halfspaces and the
shoelace summands.  A zero-length edge has \(g_j\equiv0\).  Subdividing
a collinear side replaces its support by positive multiples of the
same form.  Such a side is charging after subdivision if and only if
at least one subedge is charging: if an endpoint of the whole side
has a negative wall coordinate, the adjacent subedge has it, while
an affine coordinate cannot become negative inside a segment whose
two endpoints are nonnegative.  Hence subdivision changes neither
\(Z\) nor \(W\).

If \(g_i\) is replaced by \(\alpha_i g_i\), with
\(\alpha_i>0\), its halfspace and every line intersection are
unchanged.  Every strict sign is unchanged.  At an active zero,
\[
D(\alpha_i g_i)=\alpha_i Dg_i,
\]
even when \(\alpha_i\) varies, so equality rows and feasibility rows
change only by positive scaling.  Different valid facet selections
describe the same geometric polygon, so their shoelace expressions
agree on the common validity domain.  They therefore have the same
differential along its structural tangent space; two ambient
covectors can differ only by structural equality rows.  Reducing the
input description of \(B\) removes only zero edges, collinear
subdivision copies, and auxiliary inequalities which were never
geometric boundary facets.  Genuine facet constraints remain in
(14), including those currently redundant for \(Z\) or \(W\), so
their first possible contact is not lost.  This proves all asserted
invariances.
statement:
Write
\[
[u,v]=u_1v_2-u_2v_1,\qquad Ju=(-u_2,u_1).
\]
Use the singleton coordinates \(S=f_2,T=f_3\) and the physical-area
factor
\[
\gamma=\frac1{|\det(\nabla f_2,\nabla f_3)|}
\]
from accepted fact `82b3ba85b724a42f`.  Let
\[
B=(b_0,\ldots,b_{n-1}),\qquad b_j=(S_j,T_j),
\]
be a counterclockwise boundary list with every zero-length edge
deleted.  Put
\[
d_j=b_{j+1}-b_j,\qquad
g_j(X)=\lambda_j(X)=-[d_j,X-b_j].
\tag{1}
\]
Thus \(g_j\leq0\) on \(B\).  Set
\[
g_{\sf S}(S,T)=-S,\qquad g_{\sf T}(S,T)=-T,
\tag{2}
\]
and
\[
\mathcal J_{\rm ch}
=\{j:\min(S_j,S_{j+1})<0
\text{ or }\min(T_j,T_{j+1})<0\}.
\tag{3}
\]
For
\[
I_Z=\{{\sf S},{\sf T}\}\cup\mathcal J_{\rm ch},
\qquad
I_W=\{{\sf S},{\sf T}\}\cup\{0,\ldots,n-1\},
\tag{4}
\]
define
\[
Z=\bigcap_{i\in I_Z}\{g_i\leq0\},\qquad
W=\bigcap_{i\in I_W}\{g_i\leq0\}.
\tag{5}
\]
Then \(W=B\cap\{S,T\geq0\}\), \(W\subseteq Z\), and the zero-charge
capacity is
\[
\boxed{\mathscr C(B)=|Z\setminus W|=|Z|-|W|.}
\tag{6}
\]
Here and below area is physical planar area.  Boundaries on
\(S=0\) or \(T=0\) have zero area, so (6) is unchanged if the open
singleton chamber is used.

The following is an exact finite fixed-code formula for either
\(P=Z\) or \(P=W\).  Write every form in its coordinate coefficients,
\[
g_i(X)=n_i\mathbin{\cdot}X+c_i.
\tag{7}
\]
For the axes,
\[
(n_{\sf S},c_{\sf S})=((-1,0),0),\qquad
(n_{\sf T},c_{\sf T})=((0,-1),0),
\tag{8}
\]
and for a polygon edge,
\[
n_j=((d_j)_2,-(d_j)_1),\qquad c_j=[d_j,b_j].
\tag{9}
\]
For two nonparallel support lines put
\[
\delta_{ik}=[n_i,n_k],
\qquad
x(i,k)=
\frac1{\delta_{ik}}
\left(
(n_i)_2c_k-c_i(n_k)_2,\,
c_i(n_k)_1-(n_i)_1c_k
\right).
\tag{10}
\]

A two-dimensional bounded code for \(P\) consists of distinct
support indices \(a_0,\ldots,a_{m-1}\), \(m\geq3\), and the vertices
\[
p_\nu=x(a_{\nu-1},a_\nu)
\qquad(\nu\ {\rm mod}\ m),
\tag{11}
\]
subject to the following finite predicates:
\[
\delta_{a_{\nu-1},a_\nu}\neq0,
\qquad
\|p_{\nu+1}-p_\nu\|^2>0,
\tag{12}
\]
\[
g_{a_\nu}(p_\mu)<0
\quad
\text{if }\mu\notin\{\nu,\nu+1\},
\tag{13}
\]
and
\[
h_{\nu i}:=-g_i(p_\nu)\geq0
\quad(i\in I_P).
\tag{14}
\]
The incidences
\[
g_{a_{\nu-1}}(p_\nu)
=g_{a_\nu}(p_\nu)=0
\tag{15}
\]
are identities.  Conditions (12)--(14) imply, and are an exact
finite certificate, that
\[
P=\operatorname{conv}\{p_0,\ldots,p_{m-1}\}
\tag{16}
\]
with the displayed counterclockwise cyclic order.  Consequently
\[
|P|=\frac{\gamma}{2}
\sum_{\nu=0}^{m-1}[p_\nu,p_{\nu+1}].
\tag{17}
\]
All quantities in (10)--(17) are rational functions of the support
coefficients.  Signs may be tested polynomially by multiplying by
even powers of the nonzero denominators in (10).

Let the polygon vertices move with velocities
\(\beta_j=\dot b_j\), and put
\(\dot d_j=\beta_{j+1}-\beta_j\).  The axes have
\(\dot n=\dot c=0\), while
\[
\dot n_j=((\dot d_j)_2,-(\dot d_j)_1),
\qquad
\dot c_j=[\dot d_j,b_j]+[d_j,\beta_j].
\tag{18}
\]
For \(p_\nu=x(i,k)\), its exact velocity is the unique solution
\[
\begin{pmatrix}n_i^{\mathsf T}\\ n_k^{\mathsf T}\end{pmatrix}
\dot p_\nu
=-
\begin{pmatrix}
\dot n_i\mathbin{\cdot}p_\nu+\dot c_i\\
\dot n_k\mathbin{\cdot}p_\nu+\dot c_k
\end{pmatrix}.
\tag{19}
\]
Equivalently, for an active moving polygon edge,
\[
0=Dg_j(p_\nu)
=-[\dot d_j,p_\nu-b_j]-[d_j,\dot p_\nu-\beta_j],
\tag{20}
\]
and an active axis gives respectively
\(\dot S(p_\nu)=0\) or \(\dot T(p_\nu)=0\).
Thus wall vertices require no slope division.  Differentiating (17)
gives
\[
D|P|[\beta]
=\frac{\gamma}{2}
\sum_{\nu=0}^{m-1}
[p_{\nu-1}-p_{\nu+1},\dot p_\nu].
\tag{21}
\]
For fixed bounded codes of \(Z\) and \(W\),
\[
\boxed{
D\mathscr C(B)[\beta]
=\frac{\gamma}{2}
\sum_\nu[z_{\nu-1}-z_{\nu+1},\dot z_\nu]
-\frac{\gamma}{2}
\sum_\mu[w_{\mu-1}-w_{\mu+1},\dot w_\mu].
}
\tag{22}
\]
This is the capacity row required by accepted fact
`42e17c270e11ad3e`.

Bounded lower-dimensional codes are included as follows.  A carrier
certificate is a finite set \(A\subseteq I_P\) and positive rational
functions \(\mu_i\) satisfying the coefficient identity
\[
\sum_{i\in A}\mu_i g_i\equiv0.
\tag{23}
\]
Every feasible point then satisfies \(g_i=0\) for all \(i\in A\).
The rank of \(\{n_i:i\in A\}\) is the codimension of the carrier.
For rank one, solve one nonzero carrier equation rationally as
\[
X=X_0+tq.
\tag{24}
\]
Every remaining inequality restricts to
\[
\alpha_i t+\kappa_i\leq0.
\tag{25}
\]
A bounded one-dimensional code chooses a lower-bound index
\(\ell\) with \(\alpha_\ell<0\) and an upper-bound index \(u\) with
\(\alpha_u>0\), puts
\[
t_-=-\frac{\kappa_\ell}{\alpha_\ell},
\qquad
t_+=-\frac{\kappa_u}{\alpha_u},
\tag{26}
\]
and requires
\[
t_-<t_+,\qquad
\alpha_i t_\pm+\kappa_i\leq0\quad(i\in I_P).
\tag{27}
\]
Then \(P=[X_0+t_-q,X_0+t_+q]\).  For carrier rank two, two independent
carrier equations give one rational point \(X_0\), and the finite
conditions are \(g_i(X_0)\leq0\) for all \(i\); then \(P=\{X_0\}\).
Both cases have
\[
|P|=0,\qquad D|P|=0
\tag{28}
\]
on their persistent structural stratum.  A zero interval length or a
carrier-rank change is a recoding event, not an ambient
differentiability assertion.

The complete validity and event list is the following.

1. The input polygon predicates are
\[
\|d_j\|^2>0,\qquad
-g_j(b_k)>0\quad(k\notin\{j,j+1\})
\tag{29a}
\]
after reduction to genuine geometric facets, together with the signs
of \(S_j,T_j,S_{j+1},T_{j+1}\) which determine (3).  The adjacent
incidences \(g_j(b_j)=g_j(b_{j+1})=0\) are structural.  If a
collinear subdivision is intentionally retained, its additional zero
support incidences are structural instead of strict; otherwise the
first zero in (29a) is a polygon boundary event.

2. For a two-dimensional bounded code the rational predicates are
exactly the denominators in (12), the noncollision predicates in
(12), the strict skeleton predicates (13), and the weak
facet-vertex slacks (14).  For a lower-dimensional code they are the
coefficient identities and positive multipliers in (23), a fixed
nonzero rank minor, the signs of the one-dimensional slopes in
(25), the endpoint separation in (27), and all endpoint or point
slacks in (27).

3. A zero is a persistent structural equality precisely when the
code declares that geometric incidence for the whole stratum.  This
class contains (15), marked wall incidences, fixed shared or parallel
normal rays, coincident positive rescalings of one support, the
carrier identities (23), and any retained triple incidence.  Its
differential is an equality row.

4. Apart from the structural incidences, a zero of a weak
facet-vertex slack (14), or of its one-dimensional analogue in
(27), is an active intrinsic feasibility constraint.  Continuing
with the same formula requires
\[
Dh_{\nu i}[\beta]
=-Dg_i(p_\nu)[\beta]\geq0.
\tag{29}
\]
These rows say exactly that every redundant halfspace continues to
contain every vertex of the selected polygon.  They are the only
capacity-code feasibility rows besides \(D\mathscr C\).

5. Every other zero is an immediate boundary event: a formerly
unmarked polygon vertex reaches a wall and can change
\(\mathcal J_{\rm ch}\); an input support slack in (29a) vanishes; a
polygon edge reaches zero length; a selected intersection denominator
vanishes; two selected vertices collide; a strict skeleton slack in
(13) vanishes; a carrier multiplier or fixed nonzero rank minor
vanishes; a one-dimensional endpoint slope vanishes; or an interval
collapses.  At such a point one reduces or recodes before using
another differential formula.

Parallel and redundant lines cause no missing case.  Adjacent
selected supports cannot be parallel because of (12).  Parallel
supports which describe the same oriented line are merged, and
parallel supports at different offsets are ordered by the endpoint
slacks (14).  Oppositely oriented parallel supports can be
nonadjacent selected facets and are harmless.  Parallelism involving
only a redundant inequality is irrelevant unless one of its
facet-vertex slacks becomes zero, in which case (29) is exactly its
intrinsic row.  A repeated listed polygon vertex gives
\(d_j=0\) and \(g_j\equiv0\); deleting it changes neither (5) nor any
formula.  Consecutive collinear subdivisions give positive multiples
of one support and are merged.

For completeness, unboundedness is decided by a finite exact
predicate.  For any nonempty half-plane system let
\[
\operatorname{rec}(P)=\{r:n_i\mathbin{\cdot}r\leq0
\text{ for every }i\in I_P\}.
\tag{30}
\]
Because the normals are nonzero,
\[
\operatorname{rec}(P)\neq\{0\}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\text{for some }i\in I_P,\ \varepsilon\in\{-1,1\},
\quad
n_k\mathbin{\cdot}(\varepsilon Jn_i)\leq0
\ \text{for every }k\in I_P.
\tag{31}
\]
Thus boundedness and every bounded-to-unbounded event are determined
by finitely many determinant signs.  If \(Z\) is unbounded and
two-dimensional, then
\[
\mathscr C(B)=+\infty
\tag{32}
\]
and no finite \(C^1\) capacity row exists.  If \(Z\) is unbounded but
is persistently contained in a line, then \(W\subseteq Z\) and both
have planar area zero, so \(\mathscr C(B)=0\) on that structural
stratum; this is a separate lower-dimensional code, not the bounded
formula (17).  These are all unbounded cases.

The construction is invariant under cyclic relabeling, insertion or
deletion of repeated boundary points, subdivision or merging of a
collinear side, and positive \(C^1\) rescaling of any support
equation.  Before (3)--(5), an arbitrary description of \(B\) is
reduced to its geometric boundary facets: zero edges and nonfacet
auxiliary inequalities are deleted, while collinear subdivisions are
merged.  The genuine facet constraints in \(I_Z\) and \(I_W\) are
then all retained in (14), even when one is redundant for the
particular polygon \(Z\) or \(W\).  Any two fixed codes for the same
moving \(Z\) or \(W\) give the same area.  Their differentials agree
on the tangent space to their common structural equalities; if that
space is full-dimensional, the covectors agree outright.  At an
active zero, positive rescaling only multiplies (29) by a positive
scalar, so the intrinsic feasible tangent cone is also unchanged.
